CHART CODE
 import plotly.graph_objects as go

trade_data = {
    "Month": ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"],
    "Nigeria Exports": [15.2, 16.1, 14.8, 17.3, 18.0, 16.5, 15.8, 17.2, 16.9, 18.5, 17.8, 19.1],
    "Nigeria Imports": [6.8, 7.2, 6.5, 7.0, 7.5, 6.9, 7.1, 7.4, 6.7, 7.3, 7.0, 7.6],
    "Angola Exports": [12.5, 13.1, 12.9, 13.8, 14.2, 13.5, 14.0, 14.6, 13.9, 15.0, 14.7, 15.3],
    "Angola Imports": [4.9, 5.1, 4.7, 5.0, 5.3, 4.8, 5.2, 5.4, 5.0, 5.5, 5.1, 5.6]
}

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=trade_data["Month"],
    y=trade_data["Nigeria Exports"],
    mode='markers',
    name='Nigeria Exports',
    marker=dict(color='#e31a1c', size=10),
    line=dict(width=0)
))

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=trade_data["Month"],
    y=trade_data["Nigeria Imports"],
    mode='markers',
    name='Nigeria Imports',
    marker=dict(color='#ff7f00', size=10),
    line=dict(width=0)
))

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=trade_data["Month"],
    y=trade_data["Angola Exports"],
    mode='markers',
    name='Angola Exports',
    marker=dict(color='#33a02c', size=10),
    line=dict(width=0)
))

for i, month in enumerate(trade_data["Month"]):
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[month, month],
        y=[0, trade_data["Nigeria Exports"][i]],
        mode='lines',
        line=dict(color='#e31a1c', width=2, dash='dash'),
        showlegend=False
    ))
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[month, month],
        y=[0, trade_data["Nigeria Imports"][i]],
        mode='lines',
        line=dict(color='#ff7f00', width=2, dash='dash'),
        showlegend=False
    ))
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[month, month],
        y=[0, trade_data["Angola Exports"][i]],
        mode='lines',
        line=dict(color='#33a02c', width=2, dash='dash'),
        showlegend=False
    ))
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[month, month],
        y=[0, trade_data["Angola Imports"][i]],
        mode='lines',
        line=dict(color='#e31a1c', width=2, dash='dash'),
        showlegend=False
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    title='Monthly Trade Values for Nigeria and Angola (2023-2024)',
    xaxis_title='Month',
    yaxis_title='Value (Billion USD)',
    legend_title='Trade Type',
    template='plotly_white',
    height=600,
    width=1000
)

fig.write_image("output.png")

SUMMARY
 The chart presented is a stem plot that illustrates the monthly trade values for Nigeria and Angola over the course of a year, spanning from January to December. It compares four distinct trade categories: Nigeria’s exports, Nigeria’s imports, Angola’s exports, and Angola’s imports, each represented by differently colored markers and dashed vertical lines.

The y-axis denotes the trade values in billion USD, ranging from 0 to 20 billion, while the x-axis lists the months of the year. Each trade category is distinctly color-coded: Nigeria’s exports are shown in blue, Nigeria’s imports in orange, Angola’s exports in green, and Angola’s imports in red. The markers at the top of each dashed line indicate the exact trade values for each month.

Nigeria’s export values, the highest among the categories, generally fluctuate between approximately 14.8 billion USD and 19.1 billion USD, peaking in December. Nigeria’s imports remain relatively stable, ranging from about 6.5 billion USD to 7.6 billion USD throughout the year. Angola’s exports follow a similar but slightly lower trend compared to Nigeria’s exports, varying from 12.5 billion USD to 15.3 billion USD, with a noticeable peak in October. Angola’s imports, the lowest among the categories, range between 4.7 billion USD and 5.6 billion USD.

Overall, the chart effectively highlights the trade dynamics of both countries, showing clear visual distinctions between exports and imports and their respective values over the year.
